options: Flips `q1` (the target) if and only if `q0` (the control) is `One`
Flips `q0` if and only if `q1` is `One`
Applies a Hadamard gate to both qubits simultaneously
Measures both qubits and returns their classical values
questions.explain: CNOT is the controlled-NOT gate: the first argument is the control qubit and the second is the target; the target is flipped exactly when the control is One.

questions.q: What is the exact probability distribution over the four outcomes (00, 01, 10, 11) for the Bell pair produced by `H(q0)` followed by `CNOT(q0, q1)`, starting from `|00⟩`?
options: P(00) = 1.0, and the other three outcomes are impossible
questions.explain: Tracing the amplitudes: |00> -> H on q0 -> [1/sqrt2, 0, 1/sqrt2, 0] -> CNOT swaps the |10> and |11> slots -> [1/sqrt2, 0, 0, 1/sqrt2]. Squaring gives P(00)=0.5, P(11)=0.5, and exactly 0 for P(01) and P(10).

questions.q: What does it mean, operationally, for the two qubits in the Bell pair to be 'entangled' rather than independently random?
options: Measurement outcomes are correlated -- the two results always agree -- even though neither qubit had a definite value before measurement
Each qubit individually always measures as Zero
The two qubits must be physically adjacent on the hardware to work at all
Entanglement means the two qubits were measured at exactly the same picosecond
questions.explain: Entanglement here means the joint outcome is constrained (r0 always equals r1) even though each qubit alone still looks like a 50/50 coin flip in isolation -- there is no definite individual value before measurement, only a correlated joint one.

questions.q: If a buggy version of the lab circuit instead produced a roughly even 25/25/25/25 split across all four outcomes (00, 01, 10, 11), what would that most likely indicate?
options: The two qubits ended up independently superposed rather than entangled -- e.g. H applied to both qubits separately with no working CNOT between them
The circuit is working exactly as intended for a Bell state
The simulator ran out of memory and defaulted to random output
The Result type returned Bool instead of the expected Zero/One values
questions.explain: A 25/25/25/25 split is the signature of two independent coin flips, not entanglement -- it suggests the CNOT didn't correctly correlate the qubits (e.g. applied to the wrong qubits, or H applied to both independently instead of only the control before CNOT).

questions.q: What does `use (q0, q1) = (Qubit(), Qubit());` do, and what state do q0 and q1 start in?
options: It allocates two separate qubits in one statement, both starting in `|0⟩`
It allocates one qubit and aliases it under two names
It allocates two qubits that start already entangled with each other
It allocates two qubits starting in `|1⟩`, the opposite of the single-qubit `use` default
questions.explain: This statement allocates two independent qubits in a single use statement; like any qubit allocated with use, each starts in the |0> state -- entanglement only appears after H and CNOT are applied.
